newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Students protest against Congo's Kabila in capital.
newsitem.headline: Students protest against Congo's Kabila in capital.

text.p: Several hundred students from Kinshasa University marched in the capital on Saturday to protest against the self-proclaimed president of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Laurent Kabila, and the presence of Rwandan troops, witnesses said.
They said the crowd of protesters, who headed from the working-class Matonge district towards the city centre, was much larger than an anti-Kabila demonstration on Friday.

"We want the Rwandans to leave, Kabila has sold the country," said medical student Henri Olenga. Other students said Kabila must appoint veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi to his government.

A week ago Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) entered Kinshasa after the flight of President Mobutu Sese Seko, who dominated Africa's third largest country for over three decades.
Western intelligence sources say Kabila's seven-month rebellion, triggered by ethnic Tutsis demanding citizenship, has received military assistance from Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army.
